stories.headline: Trump takes his midterm barnstorm to Port Huron today, aiming to flip Michigan’s open Senate seat against Abdul El-Sayed
stories.summary: President Trump brings his midterm campaign swing to Port Huron, Michigan, on Sunday, a day after Barack Obama rallied Democrats in Michigan and Ohio. Republicans see a chance to win an open Senate seat in a state where the GOP hasn’t won a Senate race in more than three decades. Trump-backed former congressman Mike Rogers faces progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, a former Wayne County public health official, in the Nov. 3 race to replace retiring Democrat Gary Peters. Trump has called El-Sayed a “jihadist” and tied him to the Muslim Brotherhood, which El-Sayed rejects. In their final debate Rogers asked, “Are you for America, or are you for these terrorist groups overseas?” El-Sayed called the question “shameful.” El-Sayed has dared Trump to come (“Donald, if you’re watching, don’t wuss out, man”), and he apologized after saying “hurt people hurt people” following an attack on a Detroit-area synagogue. Rogers lost the 2024 Senate race to Elissa Slotkin by less than a point.

stories.headline: Israel votes Tuesday in its first election since October 7, and polls show ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot leading Netanyahu
stories.summary: Israel holds its first parliamentary election since the October 7, 2023 attacks on Tuesday. Thirty-nine parties are running, but the race is mostly a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Tens of thousands marched in Tel Aviv Saturday night demanding accountability for the failures behind October 7, while Likud voters at a market outside Tel Aviv called him “the king of Israel.” Netanyahu’s campaign frames the vote as existential, with posters near Gaza reading “Right or Palestine.” His main challenger is Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff whose son was killed fighting Hamas. Eisenkot left the government in 2024, accusing Netanyahu of dragging out the war. Polls show Eisenkot’s party with a clear lead, but he would likely need at least four coalition partners. Analyst Dahlia Scheindlin says he would set up an October 7 inquiry and draft the ultra-Orthodox, but wouldn’t change much on Gaza and Iran, the issues Trump cares about. Trump has endorsed Netanyahu, and she says Netanyahu could still be in office a year from now.

stories.headline: Walled-off OpenAI agents found a way to talk anyway, sending secrets through CPU cache timing with no network or shared files
stories.summary: In red-team tests described in an OpenAI blog post, AI agents placed in separate microVM sandboxes on shared hardware were asked to swap synthetic secrets without a network link or shared writable files, and they found several ways to do it. In one, an agent evicted chosen data from the CPU cache while the other timed the reloads, reading fast and slow loads as bits under a protocol the two had agreed on in advance. It’s the same cache-timing trick behind Spectre and Meltdown, except this covert channel needs two cooperating parties. Tom’s Hardware notes that a hijacked agent on a shared cloud server could in theory use the method to leak data without network monitoring ever seeing it. OpenAI ran the tests on isolated copies of its research infrastructure, using hundreds of billions of tokens. The disclosure follows earlier incidents involving its agents, including a September DNS episode that paused training for 11 days, and OpenAI now counts red-teaming with its most capable models as part of the safety case for continuing training.

stories.headline: “I beat my first body when I was 17”: a New Hampshire man pleads guilty to killing his father in 2003 after boasting to police
stories.summary: Douglas Herlihy, 40, has pleaded guilty to manslaughter in the 2003 killing of his father, Paul Herlihy, 50, in Milford, New Hampshire, and faces 12 to 24 years in state prison under a plea deal. Officers doing a welfare check found the father’s body on the kitchen floor, wrapped in carpet under a blue tarp, with blood on the cabinets, walls and ceiling. He had been beaten to death. Bloodstained carpet had been pushed out of the son’s bedroom window, and his closet door, covered by a towel, read “I WILL SEE YOU IN HELL.” Herlihy, who was 17 at the time, denied involvement for years. After a 2020 arrest he told an officer, “I beat cases. I beat my first body when I was 17!” A warrant followed in June 2025, and he was arrested in Saugus, Massachusetts. Attorney General John Formella said the case shows “the pursuit of justice does not end with the passage of time.”

stories.headline: Apple and M. Night Shyamalan win again: an appeals court upholds the jury verdict that “Servant” didn’t copy a 2013 film
stories.summary: The Ninth Circuit has upheld last year’s jury verdict for Apple, M. Night Shyamalan and the other defendants in the copyright suit over the Apple TV series “Servant.” Filmmaker Francesca Gregorini sued in January 2020, claiming the show’s first three episodes copied her 2013 film “The Truth About Emanuel.” Both stories feature a grieving mother who treats a doll as a living baby, along with a young caregiver. The suit was dismissed in 2020, revived on appeal in 2022, and lost unanimously at trial in January 2025. In its Oct. 22 decision, the appeals court rejected Gregorini’s argument that the jury instructions on whether the show’s creators could have seen her film were flawed. It also ruled that the judge could accept the unanimous verdict before answering a question the jurors had sent. The series starred Lauren Ambrose, Toby Kebbell, Nell Tiger Free and Rupert Grint.

stories.headline: Instagram finally lands on Apple TV, bringing Reels, longer creator videos and live shows to the big screen
stories.summary: Instagram now has an Apple TV app, bringing Reels, longer videos and live shows to Apple’s streaming box for the first time. You can watch creators you follow, discover new videos and pick up where you left off on another device, and Instagram pitches it as a way to watch with friends and family. Apple’s metadata dates version 66.0 to Oct. 23, and an App Store listing from Oct. 19 still showed only iPhone and iPad support. Instagram’s TV app started as a test on Amazon Fire TV in December 2025, then reached Google TV in February and Samsung TVs in June. Meta said in June it would add longer creator content, episodic series and live broadcasts. The app requires tvOS 26.0 or later. It follows Instagram’s long-requested iPad app, which arrived in September 2025.

stories.headline: November’s LEGO lineup: the record-breaking Sagrada Família, Dragon Ball’s Shenron & Goku, a Venice Icons set and Cosy Plants
stories.summary: Only a handful of LEGO sets launch in November, but they include the biggest one ever. LEGO Insiders get early access on Nov. 1, and everyone else can buy them from Nov. 4. Insiders membership is free. The headliner is 21065 Sagrada Família, the Architecture tribute to Gaudí’s Barcelona basilica, which arrives five months after its reveal as the largest LEGO set ever by piece count. Dragon Ball debuts with the Icons set 11390 Dragon Ball: Shenron & Goku, ahead of a standalone theme planned for 2027. A second Icons set recreates the Italian city of Venice and comes with November’s only gift-with-purchase, which matches the set. Botanicals adds 10371 Cosy Plants, with new accessories and a plant that breaks from the theme’s usual upright designs.

stories.headline: Nicko McBrain says Iron Maiden failed Blaze Bayley by refusing to tune the songs down for his baritone
stories.summary: Former Iron Maiden drummer Nicko McBrain, promoting his autobiography “Hello Boys And Girls!”, told Classic Album Review that the band should have helped Blaze Bayley more during his 1994–1999 run as singer. “We didn’t transpose the songs. We should have gone down a note … half a step or a full step,” he said. He noted that Bruce Dickinson’s range is “soprano, almost” while Bayley is a baritone, and that the “Virtual XI” tour “was really tough for him.” McBrain called that period “like a dark cloud” in his life. He also admitted he was the most outspoken member about how Dickinson left, announcing his exit halfway through the “Fear Of The Dark” tour, and said there was “a lot of bad blood.” He praised the 2000 reunion album “Brave New World,” recorded in Paris with producer Kevin Shirley, and the return of guitarist Adrian Smith, whom he called the band’s commercial songwriter.

stories.headline: Tracy G on quitting Dio: after six years on lead, Ronnie asked him to play rhythm, and he walked
stories.summary: Tracy Grijalva, known as Tracy G, played guitar for Ronnie James Dio from 1993 to 1999. In a preview of an upcoming Guitar World interview, he explains why he left. He auditioned twice after Dio’s second exit from Black Sabbath, got the call from drummer Vinny Appice, and debuted with Dokken bassist Jeff Pilson on 1993’s “Strange Highways,” followed by 1996’s “Angry Machines.” He says his heavier, grunge-era sound wasn’t chasing trends: “That’s just the way I play.” It ended when Dio brought back “Dream Evil” guitarist Craig Goldy on lead, which Grijalva believes management and the label wanted. “I had played guitar and lead guitar for Ronnie for six years, and now he asked me to play rhythm,” he says. “If you take that from me, then I’m out.” He insists there was no feud, but when he called Dio’s office the next Christmas to leave a holiday message, “I never heard back from him again.”

stories.headline: Houdini died 100 years ago this Halloween, and a surgeon now says the famous stomach-punch story was an insurance cover-up
stories.summary: Harry Houdini, born Erik Weisz in Hungary in 1874 and raised in Wisconsin, died 100 years ago this week at age 52. Historian Roger Dreyer says the Metamorphosis Trunk first made him bookable, and then the handcuff, straitjacket and upside-down water-tank escapes made him a legend. He later spent his final years exposing fake spiritualist mediums. The usual account says he died of appendicitis made worse by a college student’s surprise punches to his stomach. Surgeon Larrian Gillespie’s new book, “Houdini: The Man Who Died Twice,” argues his death certificate was altered and that an intestinal blockage and an unreported last-minute surgery killed him. She says his team pushed the punch story because his double-indemnity policy paid about $500,000 more, in today’s money, for an accidental death. She also argues he may have died on Oct. 30, not on Halloween. The current owner of Houdini’s Harlem townhouse is holding a séance there this weekend, as fans do every year.

stories.headline: Britain is paying $81 million for a robotic “garbage truck” with claws to grab dead satellites and drag them out of orbit
stories.summary: The UK Space Agency has picked ClearSpace UK to build a spacecraft that captures dead satellites with a robotic claw system and drags them down to burn up in the atmosphere, under a contract worth about $81 million. The Active Debris Removal mission is set to launch in 2029 from SaxaVord Spaceport in Shetland, and its first job is to remove two defunct UK satellites by 2032. The craft has to match the motion of targets that may be tumbling at around 17,000 mph. After securing one, it moves it into a lower orbit and releases it. It is being designed for refueling and reuse, so one spacecraft could clear several pieces of junk. ESA tracks about 47,140 objects in orbit and estimates there are millions of smaller fragments. Even a 1-centimeter piece can disable a spacecraft, and ESA’s 2026 report says active removal will be needed to stop collisions from multiplying the debris.

stories.headline: Ukrainian drones reportedly hit a sanctioned Russian titanium plant 1,400 km from the border, plus a missile-parts factory
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck Avisma, one of the world’s largest titanium sponge producers, in Berezniki in Russia’s Perm Krai on Sunday, according to Ukrainian and Russian monitoring channels. The plant sits more than 1,400 kilometers (870 miles) from the border. Perm Governor Dmitry Makhonin said 11 drones were downed and an unnamed industrial facility in the north of the region had “minor” damage but kept operating, with five employees injured. Avisma, part of VSMPO-AVISMA, has been under U.S. sanctions since 2023 and makes material used in military aircraft, nuclear submarines, armored vehicles and missiles. Later in the day Ukraine also reportedly attacked the Energiya plant in Yelets, Lipetsk Oblast, which makes components for missile systems and drones, more than 200 kilometers from the border.

stories.headline: Twelve people, six of them minors, are hurt in a shooting outside Florida A&M’s stadium after its homecoming game
stories.summary: Twelve people were injured, 11 of them by gunfire, when shots rang out about 8 p.m. Saturday at an intersection next to Florida A&M University’s Bragg Memorial Stadium in Tallahassee, where the historically Black university had just hosted Arkansas-Pine Bluff for its homecoming game. Three victims were seriously hurt, including one minor; six of the injured are under 18 and the youngest is 11. Police Chief Lawrence Revell called it “an isolated incident between two or three individuals” that began as an altercation, said police believe one shooter was involved, and said no one had been arrested as of early Sunday. He praised officers who carried victims in their arms because vehicles could not get through the crowd, and asked witnesses to come forward. FAMU said the shooting happened on Perry Street near campus and that the campus was safe; nearby Florida State told people to stay indoors.

stories.headline: An Ohio village’s new mosque took hundreds of thousands from Uzbek-owned trucking firms with long safety-violation records, Fox finds
stories.summary: In part two of its series on trucking fraud in southwest Ohio, Fox News Digital reports that the Islamic Center of Maineville, under construction for four years in a Warren County village of about 1,400 people, has received substantial donations from Uzbek-owned trucking companies cited for serious safety and compliance violations. The mosque’s Telegram channel, which has about 3,600 members, posted screenshots of the gifts and showed ties to people identified as current or former Uzbek officials. One Springboro carrier gave at least $28,000 across 28 donations despite English-proficiency, invalid-CDL, logging-device and hours-of-service violations; another, with more than 100 violations including unsafe driving and invalid CDLs, gave at least $25,000. Republican state Rep. Michelle Teska is pushing legislation to crack down on truck drivers who cannot speak English. Part one traced the issue to a fatal crash by an Uzbek driver.

stories.headline: Terrible Towels at the Eiffel Tower: Steelers fans turn Paris black and gold before today’s first NFL game in France
stories.summary: A huge crowd of Pittsburgh Steelers fans gathered in front of the Eiffel Tower on Saturday, waving Terrible Towels on the eve of Sunday’s historic game against the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France, the NFL’s first regular-season game in Paris. Viewer videos sent to WTAE showed the black-and-gold crowd from the tower’s base and from a nearby bridge. Kickoff is 9:30 a.m. ET; WTAE is airing the game in Pittsburgh with a pregame special starting at 7 a.m. The fan gathering came a day after the league closed its “NFL House” fan venue in the city as protests swept France.

stories.headline: Connecticut towns are banning data centers before anyone has even proposed one
stories.summary: About half a dozen Connecticut municipalities have moved to block data center development with temporary moratoriums or outright bans, according to a CT Mirror review of meetings and records, even though almost no projects have been proposed. East Lyme’s Zoning Commission unanimously adopted an indefinite ban that took effect Saturday; New Haven passed a one-year moratorium in September with an exemption for its quantum computing hub; and tiny Morris has a two-year ban. Experts say Connecticut has never been attractive for big “hyperscale” sites because of high electricity costs and the need for large plots and utility access. A 2021 sales-tax break for projects investing at least $200 million has been used only once, for Cigna’s $386 million renovation of an existing data center in Windsor, and the state has reviewed just two applications. A planned facility next to the Millstone nuclear plant in Waterford died after local pushback. Trumbull has its own hearing on a proposed one-year moratorium.

stories.headline: Soldiers guard central Milan as youth protests spread across Europe, from Rome and Turin to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana
stories.summary: Thousands of young people marched Saturday in Milan, Rome, Turin and other Italian cities as authorities flooded the streets with police and soldiers to head off a repeat of last weekend’s looting. Milan stayed peaceful, but there were brief clashes with police in Rome and Turin. Premier Giorgia Meloni sent another 500 soldiers to Milan on top of hundreds already there, backing about 5,000 police, and announced tougher penalties for minors, who police say made up much of last week’s violent crowds; several minors were detained in Milan as a precaution. Luxury boutiques including Gucci, Tiffany and Omega boarded up, and the Apple store stayed closed. Right-wing student groups also marched in Rome against the left-wing protests. Large demonstrations hit Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana as well, over issues ranging from education and corruption to anti-war causes, pensions and housing.

stories.headline: Apple says it wants to fix Safari’s cramped layout on the iPhone Duo’s outer screen — and adds book-style two-page PDFs
stories.summary: Apple is looking at ways to let websites use more of the iPhone Duo’s short, wide outer display, where Safari’s controls sit along the side and pages are currently squeezed into the area beside them. In a WebKit post on Friday, Apple’s Jen Simmons said the existing viewport-fit=cover setting could let pages extend under the controls, but Apple’s research found many sites don’t leave enough room around key content, so parts of the page would be hidden. Apple is exploring an alternative, such as letting a header’s background span the screen while its links stay clear of the controls. For now Safari 27.1 fills the leftover strip with the page’s background color. Safari 27.1 also shows PDFs as two pages when the Duo is held half-folded like a book, and developers can test experimental fold-posture detection behind feature flags.

stories.headline: Trumbull’s Kids Pumpkin Fest is Sunday on the Town Hall Green with pumpkin decorating, a live DJ and touch-a-truck
stories.summary: Trumbull’s annual Kids Pumpkin Fest runs this Sunday, Oct. 25, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. on the Town Hall Green at 5866 Main Street, Patch reports. The free family event features pumpkin decorating, face painting, lawn games, crafts and a live DJ, plus a touch-a-truck with the Long Hill Fire and Trumbull Police departments and crafts with the Trumbull Nature and Arts Center. Mobile coffee trailer Brewberry Cafe will serve a seasonal menu.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: a hearing on a one-year data center moratorium, early voting opens Monday at the library, and a Town Hall Halloween parade
stories.summary: Trumbull’s Planning and Zoning Commission will hold a public hearing Wednesday on a proposed text amendment that would define data centers as their own principal use in the town’s zoning rules and put a one-year moratorium on them, according to the meeting agenda, Patch reports in its weekly look at what’s coming up in town. Early voting for the Nov. 3 election runs Monday, Oct. 19, through Sunday, Nov. 1, at the Trumbull Library, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with longer 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. hours on Oct. 27 and Oct. 29, according to the town clerk. Patch also points to First Selectman Vicki Tesoro’s statement on the proposed high-density housing development at 1, 7 and 15 Main St. in Monroe, near the Coventry Lane area of Trumbull; no application is pending in Trumbull, and residents can send comments to the Monroe Planning and Zoning Commission. The Commission on Aging will hear an update on fraud prevention and a Senior Center report, and preschoolers can trick-or-treat through Town Hall in the annual Halloween parade, which has two sessions of 20 children each and requires registration.
